target.title: fix: stop selected channel sessions from WebChat
target.body: Supersedes #101495 Related: #91987 ## What Problem This Solves Control UI can show a channel session as active even when that run was started by Telegram, Weixin, or another channel rather than by the current browser. In that state the browser has no local run ID, so the existing stop path cannot target the selected channel session and queued follow-up work may restart after the visible run stops. ## Why This Change Was Made The stop behavior now has two explicit paths: - Browser-owned runs keep the existing run-ID-targeted **chat.abort** request. - A selected non-global session with no browser-local run ID sends **sessions.abort** with the exact session key and **clearQueued: true**. **clearQueued** is an additive, opt-in Gateway protocol field. A key-only non-global request with **clearQueued: true** discards that session's followup and lane queues before abort signals can promote queued work. Existing RPC and SDK callers that omit the field preserve their queues; **Session.abort()** still sends only **{ key }**. Explicit **runId** requests remain run-scoped. After existing agent/session resolution and abort authorization, the Gateway also stops the exact persisted embedded/channel-reply run. It does not scan hidden controllers, widen **chat.abort** ownership, or fabricate a run ID for reply-only work. Canonical **global** sessions retain their existing agent-qualified **chat.abort** behavior because the shared global queue has no safe per-agent cleanup identity. The rebase also preserves current **main**'s unknown-agent protection: unknown sessions are rejected before store creation or lifecycle cleanup, while retired agents with an existing store remain addressable. ## User Impact Typing **/stop** or pressing stop in Control UI now stops the exact selected channel session, prevents its queued successor from restarting, and leaves other channel sessions running. Existing SDK/RPC abort behavior is unchanged unless a caller explicitly opts into **clearQueued**. ## Evidence Exact reviewed head: **7c91dd204ec0be75188ee53577f1a5c489d542ee** Focused validation: - node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-abort.test.ts — 9 passed - node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.abort-agent-scope.test.ts — 29 passed - node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-authorization.test.ts — 19 passed - node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/sdk/src/index.test.ts -t "keeps key-only Session.abort compatible by omitting clearQueued" — 1 passed - node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts -t handleAbortChat — 16 passed - node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts -t "sends /stop to the exact selected channel session" — 1 passed - pnpm protocol:gen, pnpm protocol:gen:swift, and pnpm protocol:gen:kotlin reproduced committed protocol output with no drift. - Core production/test, UI production/test, and packages-test **tsgo** lanes passed. - pnpm format:check and git diff --check passed. - OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build passed on supported Node 24 arm64. - Fresh full-branch **autoreview** reported no accepted/actionable findings (patch is correct, confidence 0.87). Exact-head runtime proof used a temporary uncommitted QA Lab scenario with a real Gateway child, three qa-channel accounts, mock OpenAI, and the real browser Control UI. Both steps passed and the evidence ref is exactly **7c91dd204ec0be75188ee53577f1a5c489d542ee**: - Browser RPC included exactly sessions.abort { key: "agent:qa:direct:dm:control-ui-stop-selected", clearQueued: true } for the stop action, with no **chat.abort** or **chat.send**. - The selected session changed from **hasActiveRun: true** to **false**. - The other channel session remained **hasActiveRun: true**. - The selected session's queued successor produced 0 model requests and 0 outbound messages. GitHub Actions exact-head CI: [run 29674645937](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29674645937). Prior #101495 recordings remain useful scenario context, but are not used as current-head proof: - [Selected channel session stops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f32135-1f1a-4f9c-b0a7-ddade5464b86) - [Other channel sessions remain active](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5b78d13-90c5-416f-a354-610fef9b6c59)
